Subject: Exploring runtime embedding bridge between Redwood and Atlas SDKs

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Atlas Prompting Labs builds a dev-friendly SDK layering around embedding providers and prompt tools — our customers routinely need predictable inference cost when moving from local eval to production. We think there's a strong fit: offering an "embedding bridge" that lets Atlas SDK users route dense vector ops to Redwood's runtime (hosted or dedicated) while preserving their local instrumentation (tracing + prompts).

Attached is a short technical brief that outlines our proposal and two integration patterns (direct RPC vs. sidecar adapter). High-level asks from our side:
- A brief scoping call with Redwood infra/serving eng (30–45 min).
- A mutual action plan with milestones (proto, sandbox, perf run, go/no-go).
- An initial sense of pricing/credits for sandbox capacity.

Are you the right person to coordinate? If not, could you loop in whoever owns ISV partnerships and the runtime product?

Best,
Ethan Adler
Head of Platform Partnerships
Atlas Prompting Labs

Following up from the call notes (thanks everyone) — two quick technical clarifications from the serving/runtime side before we finalize the MAP:

1) Kernel/quantization compatibility: the Atlas brief references 4-bit quantized embedding tables and a fallback to fp16 for long-tail models. We can support that, but we need the model family names and an export of the quant config. Can you confirm whether your SDK will transmit model metadata in the handshake (name, quant config, seq len expectations)? If not, we should add a small metadata header on the RPC to avoid runtime kernel mis-selection.

2) KV caching contract: your sidecar option implies a shared KV cache (Atlas sidecar + Redwood serving). We can do an authenticated prefix cache API (simple PUT/GET semantics) but we need TTL semantics and an eviction hint. Suggested fields: cache_key, seq_prefix_hash, ttl_ms, eviction_priority (low/normal/high). Does that map to how Atlas currently indexes prefixes?

I've attached a lightweight diagram with the two patterns and where instrumentation hooks would land. If you'd rather avoid adding metadata to every call, we can implement a negotiate() RPC once per session to communicate quant/kernel choices and cache policy. That keeps per-request overhead minimal.

If Ethan/Sophia can reply to the two points above, we can update the MAP and lock the pilot milestones (sandbox perf run week, integration QA, production readiness checklist).

—Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
